chapter_title: Concerning the Seven Works of the Living Spirit

3.original: [The second: He spread about the one who had rebelled, he crucified [h]
3.content: The second: He spread about the one who had rebelled, he crucified [h

spiritual_reading:
The Divine Life acted from omnipotent love through a full series of complete operations.

First, it rescued the primary good in the human that can meet evil directly, and lifted it from the level of outer memory-knowledges where it had been submerged, bringing it into clearer intelligence and safer reception.

Second, it encompassed the ruling defection of the selfhood, exposed it to the full judgment of truth in every level of the human, and fixed it in the outermost degree so that it could no longer dominate from within.

Third, it subdued, gathered into order, and opened to examination the compounded interiors of spiritual death, so that their hidden structure might be made manifest and their power broken.

Fourth, it formed orderly vehicles of enlightened truth by which higher wisdom could be carried into lower degrees without being lost, dispersed, or profaned.

Fifth, it called forth a sufficient complement of operative powers and set them in their appointed functions. These took possession of the ultimate boundary of the created order and sustained the whole arrangement under its total pressure. It also brought forth the full series of living utterances of Divine truth across the discrete degrees, fixing them in the containing forms proper to each degree, and setting an additional governing utterance into the dominating natural power. Again it brought forth a directed impulse of communication, so that it might be conjoined with the sufficient enlightened agencies for effect in ultimates.

Sixth, once the ultimate boundary had been established, it rose into clearer exertion and sent out an abundance of powers and many ministering intelligences, that they might set limits on every side, protecting the whole circuit until the arrangement of all uses was completed. When the works were brought to their end, it took some of these into interior preservations, and it stationed others in fixed outer functions to maintain vigilance.

Seventh, at the time when Divine truth in a mediating form manifested a glorious revelation suited to reception, the Divine Life established many goods and many ministering intelligences. Their further action here is unclear because the text is broken; it appears they were made to take firm hold of the established arrangement so that the entire ordered structure would not turn its forces against heavenly wisdom, but remain in subordination to it under the light that proceeds from the Divine.

In addition, a further great and glorious operation is to be accomplished at the completion of the age: the final formed state of the regenerated human, which will be lifted into the heavenly degrees of wisdom and love. The remaining description is fragmentary; it suggests an entering into the last state, a firm grasping of what must be held, the striking down of what resists, the rebuilding of what must be reordered, and the binding into unity of the powers that are to remain in that perfected form.

fills.fill: The second: He spread about the one who had rebelled, he crucified h
fills.notes: The seventh-works schema is formulaic in this substrate: each work begins with an ordinal tag, then a cosmic action. The ‘rebelled one’ is the bound Archon of the mixture; ‘crucified’ here is the fixing of that ruling defection into extension and ultimates (the cross as ultimate boundary) so it cannot rule inwardly.

This clause marks a second evocation within the fifth work: after sons and living words, a further ‘summons’ is called forth so it can be conjoined with the five luminous agencies in the zone. The oldest-layer logic is functional and serial, not hortatory.

fills.fill: were set over the zone and over its circuit
fills.notes: The seventh work continues the boundary-and-stability theme of the sixth: once revelation is shown, additional goods and angels are installed as superintending powers, specifically ‘over the zone’ (ultimate boundary) and its circuit, to keep the ordering from collapsing into counter-action.

This supplies the required purposive hinge before ‘They took hold of it’: the powers are made to stand in stability, then they ‘take hold’ (fasten, maintain) of the established structure. The spiritual sense demands a stabilization function rather than moral exhortation.

The following clause reads ‘not […] one another against the light’; correspondentially this is the prevention of inversion, i.e., the ordered parts turning into mutual hostility. A short governing connector like ‘that it would’ is demanded here.

The close ‘which he had …’ requires a prior act of establishment. In the oldest-layer register the light is not ‘given’ devotionally but ‘set’ or ‘appointed’ as the ruling order. This matches the spiritual constraint: subordination under proceeding light.
After ‘which he will bring up to the aeons of light; and he … in,’ the spiritual sequence requires ‘enter’ as the act of coming into the final formed state, before ‘takes hold’ and ‘smites’.
The verbs ‘takes hold’ and ‘smites’ need an object in the opposite sense: resistive forces within the mixed order that must be struck down for the final formed state to be stable.
Following ‘he builds’ the next required operation is re-ordering, not moral ‘saving’: the substrate describes structural rearrangement leading to a perfected form.
Final verb before ‘them’ must denote conjunction into unity. ‘binds them’ fits the correspondential endpoint: powers remaining are held together in the last formed state.

assessment: Most lacunae are minor letter-restorations and are secure. The only substantial gaps are in ¶8 and ¶9; these are constrained by the chapter’s correspondential structure (boundary, stabilization under light; then final-state grasping, striking, rebuilding, and binding). Exact wording remains somewhat open, but the restored phrases are aligned to the oldest-layer impersonal cosmological register and the serial logic of the seven works and the final operation.
